text: Danish general practice study by Rune Aabenhus (University of Copenhagen) characterised antibiotic prescriptions for acute respiratory tract infections via clinical-indication-labeled electronic prescriptions (retrospective registry cohort, July 2012–June 2013). Of 456,532 prescriptions, pneumonia was the most common indication (178,354; 39%), followed by acute tonsillitis (21%) and acute otitis media (19%). Penicillin V accounted for 58%, macrolides 18%, amoxicillin 15%. Second-line agent use rose with age, exceeding 40% in patients >75 years. Women were prescribed antibiotics more often regardless of indication. The first Danish study linking prescriptions to clinical indications, it confirms penicillin V as most-prescribed but finds second-line agents overused. Improved prescribing quality is warranted for pneumonia, otitis media and rhinosinusitis, plus further analysis of out-of-hours clinics.
